page_title: Living guidelines for generative AI — why scientists must oversee its use

summary.name: Living guidelines for generative AI
summary.one_liner: A Nature comment (2023) arguing that an independent scientific body should test and certify generative AI and that scientists must oversee its use in research.
use_cases: Reading a policy argument on how scientists should oversee generative AI
Finding references on AI governance and research integrity
Understanding proposals for certifying generative AI systems
Researching risks of generative AI to science and public trust
summary.what_it_does: The page is a Nature Comment from 2023 that argues generative AI systems, such as those that produce text, images, video and code from prompts, can make information more accessible and speed up technology development but also pose risks. It calls for establishing an independent scientific body to test and certify generative AI before it damages science and public trust. The page lists its reference list, which includes works on AI risk management (NIST AI RMF 1.0), research fraud, and conflicts of interest. The visible text does not describe a software tool, and the full guideline content sits behind a paywall in the excerpt provided.
notable: Proposes an independent scientific body to test and certify generative AI
Authored by a group of co-developers of living guidelines, with affiliations in the supplementary information
Cites the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and research-fraud literature
caveats: Full article text is behind a subscription paywall in the page excerpt
Describes a proposal rather than a released tool or implemented guidelines
